newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Senate speaker Petre Roman said the U.S. administration could present today its position on NATO's expansion.
Roman said the adoption by the U.S. House of Representatives of a resolution supporting Romania to join NATO in a first wave was a "big success" .
* Romania's upper Senate house adopted a law to return Greek Catholic churches confiscated by the former Communists.
* Romanian and Flemish government representatives signed a five-year cooperation accord to boost bilateral ties.
* Jiu Valley coal miners seek a 40 percent pay rise and the sacking of the local mines' manager and union leader.

* Romanian army chief of staff General Constantin Degeratu said Romania's non-admission to NATO would be a strategic error. He said Romania had proved its capacity to comply with NATO standards by joining peacekeeping missions in Angola, Bosnia and Albania.
* Poland's Foreign Minister started a two-day visit here. He will meet his Romanian counterpart Adrian Severin and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
* National Liberal Party proposed Sorin Botez as new public information minister, to replace Radu Boroianu who has been appointed Romania's ambassador to Switzerland.

* Over 5,000 construction workers marched through Bucharest asking for money to complete unfinished buildings. They handed the government a list of 20 proposals aimed to revigorate investment in the sector.
